problem:
Consider the matrix 
$W=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 2 \\ -6 & 9 & -2 \\ 8 & -12 & 10\end{aligned}].$ 
Find a basis $B$ of  $\text{Col}(W).$
worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(W),$ we reduce the matrix $W$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 2 \\ -6 & 9 & -2 \\ 8 & -12 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 8 & -12 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${w}_{1}$ and ${w}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(W)$ is ${{w}_{1},{w}_{3}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6 \\ 8\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}.
$$
